_instructions: Dominion Energy Virginia (Virginia Electric and Power Company). Parameters sourced from SCC Case PUR-2025-00058 (final order November 2025), PJM BRA reports 2025, Dominion 10-K 2025, and Schedule 1 tariff effective January 2026. rate_base_start_m and annual_capex_m are anchored to 10-K/8-K data (see _rate_base_note, _capex_note). Four remaining fields marked _VERIFY require confirmation from the SCC rate case filing before results should be trusted.
name: Virginia Electric and Power Company (Dominion Energy Virginia)
territory: Most of Virginia and parts of North Carolina
filing_case: SCC Case PUR-2025-00058 (biennial review, final order November 2025, rates effective January 2026 and January 2027)
_rate_base_note: Virginia base rate base $13.8B per Dominion 8-K investor presentation (2024E). This is the distribution base rate component excluding transmission rider ($11.8B) and generation/renewable riders ($10.5B). Distribution PP&E gross $17,261M per 10-K December 2024. Confirmation of regulatory rate base vs book value from SCC filing still useful.
_capex_note: Distribution-only CAPEX estimated at $1,600M/yr: Virginia base rate base grows ~$560M/yr net (13.8B to 16.6B over 5 years per 8-K), implying gross CAPEX of ~$1,400-1,800M after depreciation of ~$800-900M/yr on $13.8B base at ~6% depreciation rate. Total Dominion CAPEX plan is $55B/5yr=$11B/yr but this includes generation, offshore wind, and transmission. NWS-eligible share of $1,600M distribution CAPEX still needs IRP validation.
_revenue_VERIFY: SCC approved base rate revenue increases of $565.7M for 2026 and $209.9M for 2027. Total electric revenue requirement including all riders estimated at $8-10B. NEEDS VERIFICATION FROM SCC FILING.
_tariff_note: Schedule 1 (Residential Service) effective January 2026. Basic customer charge $7.58/month. Blended all-in rate approximately 14.67 cents/kWh. Virginia is partially restructured — majority of customers take bundled service. Delivery and supply split estimated from SCC filing; riders (fuel, offshore wind, grid transformation) add significantly to the blended rate.
_capacity_note: PJM DOM zone is transmission-constrained due to data centre concentration in Northern Virginia. 2025/2026 BRA: DOM zone cleared at $444.26/MW-day vs $269.92 RTO-wide. 2026/2027 BRA: DOM zone cleared at $329.17/MW-day (system-wide cap). Anchor: $329.17 x 365 / 1,000,000 = $0.120M/MW-year. Growth assumption higher than NYISO (5%/yr real) reflecting data centre load tightening reserve margins. Sources: PJM 2025/2026 BRA Report July 2024; PJM 2026/2027 BRA Report July 2025.
_dc_note: Virginia data centre operational capacity ~5,926 MW in 2024 per AAF/Virginia DEQ data; using 5,500 MW as Dominion-system estimate. dc_load_growth_rate calibrated to 4%/yr (down from an initially-proposed 8-12%/yr, which is directionally consistent with near-term data centre buildout pace but compounds to an implausible ~37,000-83,000+ MW data-centre segment alone by 2050 under this model's pure-exponential, no-saturation growth curve over a 24-year horizon). 4%/yr produces a 2050 total system peak of ~38,000 MW, consistent with the Dominion 2024 IRP range (~17,000 MW in 2022 to ~29,000 MW in 2045, roughly 70% growth). This is a modelling-horizon calibration, not a data centre industry growth forecast — real data centre buildout is expected to ramp faster than 4%/yr near-term and plateau as land/power/interconnection availability saturates, a dynamic this model's constant-rate exponential does not capture. Source: AAF April 2026; PJM 2026/2027 BRA Report; Virginia Business Feb 2026; Dominion 2024 IRP. dc_load_growth_annual retained for backward compatibility.
_property_tax_VERIFY: Virginia utility property assessed by local commissioners of revenue. Effective rates vary by locality. Estimated 1.5-2.0% of distribution rate base. NEEDS VERIFICATION FROM DOMINION ANNUAL REPORT OR SCC TESTIMONY.
_nws_VERIFY: NWS eligibility lower than NY utilities: large share of CAPEX is transmission not distribution; offshore wind and CVOW are not NWS-addressable; data centre driven transmission upgrades (89 projects per 2024 IRP) are not distribution NWS. Starting estimate 20-25% of total CAPEX is distribution NWS-eligible. MOST UNCERTAIN PARAMETER — review against IRP capital breakdown before modelling.
_grid_utilization_VERIFY: This analysis does not use actual Dominion grid utilization, hosting-capacity, or feeder-loading data — the NWS-eligible CAPEX share above (and its ceiling) is a system-wide estimate, not a measurement of real spare grid capacity anywhere on Dominion's network. If Dominion or the SCC publishes actual grid utilization data (e.g. feeder-level hosting capacity, loading, or constraint maps), it should replace this assumption. NEEDS REAL GRID UTILIZATION DATA.
_dist_upgrade_VERIFY: Northern Virginia (data centre corridor) has dense suburban/urban network approaching Con Edison cost levels. Rest of Dominion territory predominantly overhead suburban and rural, similar to RG&E. Blended estimate $1.5-2.0M/MW. NEEDS VERIFICATION FROM SCC CAPITAL FILINGS.
_class_shares_note: EIA Form 861, 2024 (Sales_Ult_Cust_2024.xlsx), Virginia Electric & Power Co, VA + NC: bundled (Part A) + delivery-only (Part C) rows, so retail-choice load is included. Residential sales 30,307,702 of 98,637,838 MWh = 30.7%; residential customers 2,492,204 of 2,783,257 = 89.5%. VA and NC rows combined (this JSON covers both). Used only when CAPACITY_SAVINGS_ALLOCATION = 'sales_share' (CORRECTED): the residential capacity credit is scaled by sales share / customer share.

starting_bill.notes: Vertically integrated: generation, fuel and transmission are utility charges, not third-party supply. Several riders changed after 1 Jul 2026 (T1, RPS, OSW, SNA, SMR, C1A, C4A on 1 Sep 2026), so line totals differ from the York County breakdown. PJM capacity costs are embedded in base generation and fuel (Dominion has proposed moving them into the fuel factor). Local consumer utility taxes vary by locality and are excluded. Annual DSM spend not filled (SCC rider orders not read).

forward_assumptions._note: Forward assumptions for the layer engine (engine/layers.py). v1.0 / CORRECTED do not read this section. Levels: for layer assumptions 'low' gives customers a SMALLER shared-savings effect and 'high' a LARGER one. For growth assumptions (projection, system_needs, capacity price growth) low/high = lower/higher growth. Scenarios (Cautious / Central / Ambitious) set the programs, deferral and utilisation layers together and hold growth assumptions and the utility share at central.

Cautious.description: Low flexible MW and EE savings, high cost per kW-year, high capitalised share, low locational match and utilisation; growth and utility share central.

Ambitious.description: High flexible MW and EE savings, low cost per kW-year, low capitalised share, high locational match and utilisation; growth and utility share central.

capacity_carve_out.source: Price: DOM zone 2026/27 BRA $329.17/MW-day. Peak: Dominion_VA.json. Residential share and customers: EIA-861 2024 (VA + NC). Scaling: PJM FPR 0.9401.
capacity_carve_out.split_note: Where capacity sits: purchased capacity expense is recovered in base rates (base generation). Dominion's 2025 fuel filing proposed moving it to the fuel factor from Jan 2026 and attributed $1.98/month (1,000 kWh) of the fuel increase to capacity (Cardinal News / SCC filings). Heatmap reports the SCC rejected the shift; an SCC order describes a change in timing only. Split used: $1.98 of $23.21 (8.5%) in fuel, the rest (91.5%) in base generation. Most of Dominion's capacity is self-supplied by owned plant whose cost is in base generation.
capacity_carve_out.method: Residential capacity obligation per customer = peak_mw x residential_share x obligation_scaling / residential_customers; $/month = obligation (kW) x price ($/kW-day) x 365/12. Assumes the residential share of the obligation equals its share of sales (residential load is peakier, so this likely understates it). The amount is moved out of the parent line(s); the total bill is unchanged.
